summary: Conviction based solely on single eyewitness testimony; identification parade invalidated due to prior exposure of accused to witness; no corroborating evidence linking appellant to murder; conspiracy theory rejected by High Court; prosecution fails to meet beyond reasonable doubt standard; circumstantial evidence chain incomplete; reliance on Anil Phukan (1993) on single witness reliability; Suresh case (2000) on identification parade purpose; Gireesan Nair (2023) on pre-parade exposure rendering identification inconsequential; appeal allowed despite concurrent trial and high court findings; miscarriage of justice avoided by granting benefit of doubt.
final_judgment: Appeal allowed; conviction and life sentence for Section 302 IPC set aside; appellant acquitted.
